name: Pandemic institutional messaging
description: The concentrated 2020–2021 repertoire of institutional reassurance, procedural qualification, and remote-meeting intervention.
cause_of_death: Public nominations and contemporary linguistic criticism documented fatigue with repeated reassurance and operational catchalls; the routine vocabulary remained available.

sources.title: COVID-19 Terminology Tops Lake Superior State University Annual Banished Words List
sources.note: Inspected original press-release PDF. Records 1,450-plus nominations, including pandemic phrases, and explains criticism of excessive corporate and public messaging.

sources.title: Lake Superior State University Banishes Familiar but Problematic Words and Terms for 2022
sources.note: Inspected original press-release PDF. Identifies new normal, you are on mute, and supply-chain explanations as pandemic-linked overuse.

sources.title: LSSU releases 2022 Banished Words list
sources.note: Independent contemporary coverage corroborates the university list and its publication date.

variants: we are all in this together
entries.gloss: A solidarity formula used to frame a shared burden or collective effort.

examples.text: We're all in this together; thank you for covering my shift.

entries.rationale: This is the pandemic messaging sense of an older expression, not a claim of lexical invention in 2020. LSSU documents concentrated adoption and backlash in 2020–2021. The peak and fade are explicitly estimated cultural-salience parameters; a banishment nomination does not establish extinction. The source specifically criticizes this phrase or its listed base expression.
